output.summary: The turnover rise is real: it reconciles to payroll, and Cedar Hollow's rise (28% to 47%) far exceeds peers' (33% to 38%), so it is not an HRIS artifact or only the labor market. Monthly separations stepped up in March 2026, when the two-Saturday policy took effect at all branches. That is before ShiftWise went live in April, and ShiftWise does not show a visible extra step. Pay was cited at similar rates in both years, and current market position is unknown. The manager-of-record field is stale, so the manager hypothesis cannot be tested, and A2 would punish the wrong people. Get branch-level data, the ShiftWise comparison and a market benchmark before committing to a 15% raise, which is irreversible and costs $2.6M a year.
